This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.

if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
This design: AREA 0, as LibreLane had it until 3.1.0.dev4 made DELAY 4
the default; DELAY 4 buffered and duplicated logic into 29% more cells.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
This design: 20 ns (50 MHz). v1.4, with its program in flip-flops,
needed 25. With the SRAM macros, layouts at 25, 20 and 16 ns all met
timing at every corner, the slow corner with about 9, 4 and under 1 ns
between flip-flops to spare; 20 keeps a margin.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
======== SPIKE: IHP SRAM macros (RM_IHPSG13_1P_256x16_c2_bm_bist), one per thread ========
Integration from https://github.com/TinyTapeout/ttihp-cmos5l-sram-example (Apache-2.0):
librelane_plugin_sram_pdn.py, odb_stripes.py, src/pdn_cfg.tcl, src/sram_bb.v, test/sram_model.
Insert the Project.ExtendPowerStripes step (librelane_plugin_sram_pdn.py) after the PDN generator.
Both at the bottom left, flipped (FS) so their pins face up towards the logic.
x = 3.36 + n x 11.24 um keeps each macro's power columns under the PDN stripes (n = 0 and 24).
The SRAM has two supply rails (VDD!, VDDARRAY!) and one ground rail (VSS!).
PDN: pdngen skips the SRAMs; ExtendPowerStripes powers them.
pdngen checks the SRAM's power connections before ExtendPowerStripes makes them, so errors are expected at this stage.
Magic DRC flags many errors inside the SRAM macro; the Tiny Tapeout precheck runs the full KLayout deck on the final GDS.
Magic extracts the SRAM from its LEF abstract, so the power stripes crossing the macro's
Metal4 obstruction show up as illegal overlaps (there is no metal there in the GDS).
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
